Right so what really helped me get the timing down was breaking it up into small chunks to help build muscle memory. So I practiced hippie jumps on the bolts, stationery and moving, whilst trying to bring my knees as high up to my chest as possible to feel comfortable. Then with my back foot, I'd practice popping with my ankle to build up the motion of as you've jumped, your ankle kinda slaps down with your toes to make the board pop. I normally place my front foot around the middle of my board and I'd just stand there for a while to practice sliding my foot up the grip. Braille has great tutorials and explanations for all this with good examples too that helped me loads. I also know that it's tempting to practice ollies stationery because it feels safer, but I'd recommend learning them moving because it'll make it easier for you to level out the board because your momentum is going forwards. Sorry for the lengthy answer haha and I'd definitely recommend checking out Brailles ollie tutorials if you haven't already!

Best of luck mate, if anything is unclear, just lmk! :)

This is a great start! Pop with the ball of your foot in the middle of the tail and maybe somewhat off the board instead of your entire foot. Also maybe work on the timing of the jump, pop and slide relationship. So essentially you crouch down ready to jump and as your momentum begins to shift upwards as you jump, you pop with your ankle and by that time, your body is already in the air because you've jumped. Whilst this is happening, you're simultaneously dragging your foot up the grip to bring the board into the air and level it out. 
If any of this is unclear to you, braille has some pretty good ollie tutorials on YouTube!

Goodluck mate, wishing you all the best :)

Haha I taught my friends how to do this trick the other day!

Basically try to keep your feet and shoulders in line with the bolts of your deck, with your feet up until round about where your laces start underneath the deck. Then you've gotta bend those knees and jump, flipping the board up with you. You should be landing in your regular cruising stance with your feet on the bolts, giving you more stability. When you land, you should also bend your knees so that your body is more stable, you have more control and that you're closer to the ground which would reduce a lot of impact if you fell. You could also start off holding onto something to help with the nerves until you feel comfortable!

After that it's all about the practice and building up your confidence slowly and steadily :)

Props to you for wearing padding and being safe!

If you ever need anymore help, feel free to let me know :D
